audit.cfg_summary: Straight-line function: segment load, two byte reads, word result construction, one far return. The entire target contains no conditional/loop/switch/indirect branch and no call.

reads: One read of the 16-bit based segment global g_8DFC (DS:0x8DFC), used as ES for both accesses.
Unsigned byte at ES:off and unsigned byte at ES:(off+1 mod 65536).
writes: No data-memory writes. Prologue saves BP; epilogue restores it. No caller argument is modified.
memory_state.return: 16-bit word (first byte << 8) | second byte; first byte is the high-order byte and the following based-segment byte is low-order.

constants_widths_pointer_arithmetic.widths_signedness: off is a signed 16-bit C int but is consumed as its 16-bit offset bit pattern. SONG yields unsigned char and promotes to 16-bit int. The source shift can form bit patterns 0x8000..0xff00, beyond signed-int range; the historical MSC 16-bit lowering supplies the observed 16-bit result bits (as the target register construction does). This is a compiler-model assumption, not a portable ISO-C shift guarantee.
constants_widths_pointer_arithmetic.pointer_math: SONGP(off) is an unsigned-byte _based(g_8DFC) pointer. Target loads at ES:BX then ES:BX+1; effective-address addition wraps the 16-bit offset within the same ES segment and does not carry into a different segment. C off+1 is evaluated as a 16-bit int by the pinned MSC compiler and its low word matches the target for all 16-bit offsets, including 0x7fff -> 0x8000 and 0xffff -> 0x0000; the latter is signed-safe (-1+1), while 0x7fff+1 relies on MSC word-wrap behavior.
constants_widths_pointer_arithmetic.constants: Byte shift 8; byte width 8; result width 16. There are no table/index scale constants, loops or calls.

static_axes.algorithm: Original moves the first byte to the high result byte and the second byte to the low result byte; source SONG(off)<<8 | SONG(off+1) is the same byte order and bit construction under MSC 16-bit target semantics.
static_axes.control_flow: No conditional, loop, switch, computed jump or alternate return exists; branch_map is empty because the full CFG is straight-line.
static_axes.memory: Exactly two based-segment byte reads, same segment, second effective offset wrapping modulo 2^16; no writes.
static_axes.return_abi: int far word return; BP is restored and far return consumes no args.
static_axes.completeness_basis: Static comparison accounts for every instruction in the 25-byte context and the whole source expression, including byte order, offset width and based-segment carry behavior.

remaining_differences.explanation: The registered dossier notes different AH/AL assignment/code shape while both target and natural C read the high byte then low byte using 16-bit based-pointer wrap. The register construction and source shift/OR produce the same 16-bit word for the supported MSC target model; no data write or call difference remains.

review_notes: Input domain pins g_8DFC to an accessible 64 KiB segment and includes every 16-bit offset, including 0xffff; malformed segment pointers are excluded.

The source expression relies on MSC 6.00AX 16-bit behavior both for left-shifting promoted unsigned-char values >=0x80 into the signed-int high bit and for off+1 at 0x7fff. The original disassembly directly specifies the returned bits and same-segment offset wrap; neither operation is being claimed portable under abstract ISO C overflow/shift rules.
